findings.title: A sign-in code was written to the log when a registered mail relay refused
findings.exploit: Relay returns failure -> the code was printed through the console sender -> platform log -> anyone or any agent that reads the aggregated logs can sign in as that user.
findings.resolution: FIXED on this branch (a3e717636): the failure path logs that nothing was sent and nothing else; pinned by tests/unit/test_email_relay.py.

findings.title: GET /api/onboarding/first-run called a get_or_create accessor (the #2669 class)
findings.exploit: Any authenticated GET mints the durable installation id as a side effect of looking.
findings.resolution: FIXED on this branch (fcfd3aa0e): reads with get_installation_id(); test_2669_minting_accessor_callers.py green.

findings.title: Links supplied by a remote service were bound to href / window.open without a scheme check
findings.exploit: A javascript: address in a terms or checkout link runs in the admin's session on click.
findings.resolution: FIXED on this branch (fcfd3aa0e): webLink() admits http(s) only; pinned by assistantCards.spec.js.

hypotheses.title: The relay seam hands a sign-in code to whatever module registered
hypotheses.note: By design: a registered relay receives the code in order to send it. Whether a deployment accepts that trust is an operator decision recorded with the private module's review.

coverage_gaps: Route-census and real-app guards (test_2996_*, test_3180_*, test_ent719_*, and others that import main) could not run locally: the host Python lacks opentelemetry.exporter. They run in CI and must be green there before merge.
No dependency scanner ran: the diff changes no lockfile, requirements file or Dockerfile.
